name: RETRIEVAL
label: Month 2 · RAG and the evals that prove it works
goal: Ingest documents AND measure whether retrieval actually works. This month makes your resume.

weeks.title: Embeddings and chunking
weeks.why: Chunking is the highest-leverage, least-discussed variable in RAG. Most broken RAG systems are broken here, not at the model. Your HuggingFace background means you can run all of this locally for zero rupees.

tasks.t: What an embedding actually is: a vector, cosine similarity, why 'similar' != 'relevant'
Run sentence-transformers locally: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Compare speed and quality. Zero API cost.
Read the MTEB leaderboard properly — understand what the retrieval column means and why the top model is not always your model
Chunking strategies: fixed-size, recursive-character, structure-aware (markdown/HTML headers), semantic. Implement all four.
Overlap, and chunk metadata (source, page, section, date) — metadata is what makes filtering and citations possible
Document parsing reality: PDFs are hostile. Try pymupdf4llm, unstructured, docling. Pick your poison.
BUILD: an ingestion pipeline over a real corpus (your company docs, or a public dataset). Output chunk-count/size distributions per strategy.

weeks.title: Vector search — build it, then adopt it
weeks.why: Write cosine similarity in numpy first. It is 15 lines, and after that no vector database is mysterious — they are all indexes plus filtering plus ops. Then learn pgvector, because you know SQL and most companies already run Postgres.

tasks.t: Brute-force search in numpy: normalise, dot product, argsort top-k. 15 lines. This is your mental model forever.
Why brute force stops working: ANN, HNSW, IVF. Understand the recall/latency tradeoff conceptually.
FAISS locally — flat vs HNSW index, measure the recall difference
pgvector on Postgres — your highest-employability option. Docker it, index it, query it with SQL you already know.
Metadata filtering — pre-filter vs post-filter, and why post-filtering silently destroys recall
Hybrid search: BM25 (rank_bm25) + dense, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Hybrid beats dense-only on most real corpora.
BUILD: the same corpus queryable through 3 backends behind one interface, plus a hybrid retriever

resources.label: Qdrant — hybrid search and RRF explained
Supabase — pgvector + free Postgres (doubles as your study-site DB)

code.label: Vector search from scratch — the whole idea, no library
code.body:
import numpy as np

class TinyVectorStore:
    def __init__(self):
        self.vecs, self.docs = None, []

    def add(self, embeddings, docs):
        e = embeddings / np.linalg.norm(embeddings, axis=1, keepdims=True)
        self.vecs = e if self.vecs is None else np.vstack([self.vecs, e])
        self.docs.extend(docs)

    def search(self, q, k=5):
        q = q / np.linalg.norm(q)
        sims = self.vecs @ q              # cosine, because everything is normalised
        idx = np.argpartition(-sims, k)[:k]
        idx = idx[np.argsort(-sims[idx])]
        return [(self.docs[i], float(sims[i])) for i in idx]

# That is a vector database. Everything else is indexes, filters, and ops.

weeks.title: RETRIEVAL EVALS — the differentiator week
weeks.why: This is the most important week in the entire roadmap. Everyone has a RAG chatbot. Almost nobody can say 'recall@5 went from 0.61 to 0.84'. Do not optimise anything before this week — you would be guessing. Implement the metrics by hand before touching Ragas, so you know what the numbers mean.

tasks.t: Build a golden set: 50-100 (question -> relevant chunk ids) pairs. Generate candidates with an LLM, then HAND-VERIFY every one. This is the work. It is boring. Do it.
Implement Recall@k and Hit Rate by hand. Understand why recall matters more than precision for the retrieval stage.
Implement MRR and nDCG@k by hand. nDCG is the one interviewers ask about; know why discounting by rank matters.
Run the baseline. Write the numbers down. Commit them to the repo. This is your 'before'.
Now try Ragas — compare its numbers against your hand-rolled ones and reconcile any difference
Build a failure taxonomy: for every miss, label WHY (bad chunking / embedding mismatch / vocabulary gap / document genuinely absent). Count them.
Read Hamel Husain on evals. Then re-read it. This is the mindset the job is actually about.

weeks.title: Reranking and query transformation — produce the 'after' number
weeks.why: Now you optimise, because now you can measure. Reranking is usually the single biggest quality jump in RAG. Every change this week gets re-measured against Week 7's baseline. At the end you have the sentence that gets you interviews.

tasks.t: Cross-encoders vs bi-encoders — why reranking is expensive but far more accurate
Run BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 locally (free, HuggingFace). Retrieve top-50, rerank to top-5. Measure.
Query expansion / multi-query: generate 3 paraphrases, retrieve for each, fuse with RRF. Measure.
HyDE — embed a hypothetical answer instead of the question. Measure. (It sometimes hurts. Report that honestly.)
Query decomposition for multi-hop questions. Measure.
Ablation table: run every combination, record recall@5 / nDCG@10 / latency / cost for each row
MILESTONE: write the before/after table into your README. This is the resume line.

code.label: The table that goes in your README (and your resume)
code.body:
## Retrieval evaluation

Corpus: 4,200 chunks / 118 documents. Golden set: 87 hand-verified queries.

| Configuration                        | Recall@5 | nDCG@10 | p95 latency | $/1k queries |
|--------------------------------------|----------|---------|-------------|--------------|
| Dense only (bge-small, 512 chunk)    | 0.61     | 0.58    | 90 ms       | $0.02        |
| + structure-aware chunking           | 0.68     | 0.64    | 90 ms       | $0.02        |
| + hybrid BM25 (RRF)                  | 0.74     | 0.70    | 130 ms      | $0.02        |
| + cross-encoder rerank (top-50 -> 5) | **0.84** | **0.81**| 380 ms      | $0.02        |
| + HyDE                               | 0.83     | 0.80    | 1,100 ms    | $0.31        |

**Shipped:** hybrid + rerank. HyDE was reverted — no recall gain, 3x latency, 15x cost.

<!-- Reporting the thing that DIDN'T work is what makes this credible. -->

weeks.deliverable: A README ablation table showing measured improvement, including at least one change you reverted because the data said so.
weeks.checkpoint: Say out loud, in one sentence: 'I improved recall@5 from X to Y by doing Z.' If you cannot, Month 2 is not finished.
